title: "Expert System"
description: "A program that applies encoded domain knowledge and rules to make recommendations or conclusions."
term: "Expert System"
letter: "E"
category: "AI Fundamentals"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

An expert system uses explicit knowledge and rules to solve problems in
a specific domain. It can apply those rules to facts and provide a
recommendation or conclusion.

## Technical explanation

Traditional expert systems commonly separate a knowledge base, such as
facts and rules, from an inference engine that applies those rules.
Systems may use forward chaining, backward chaining, or other reasoning
strategies. Their conclusions depend on the coverage and quality of the
encoded knowledge.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Expert systems illustrate a symbolic approach to AI and remain useful
when rules need to be explicit, auditable, and stable. They can also be
combined with statistical models, though rule maintenance and knowledge
coverage require ongoing work.

## How it works

The system receives facts, matches them against rules, and applies
inference steps to derive conclusions or recommendations. It may explain
which rules fired, depending on its implementation.

## Practical example

A troubleshooting system can apply rules such as “if the device will not
start and the indicator is off, check the power supply” to guide a user
through a known diagnostic process.

## Common misconceptions

- Expert systems do not necessarily learn from data.
- Rule-based does not mean error-free; rules may be incomplete,
  contradictory, or outdated.
- An expert system is not the same as a modern language model, though
  applications can combine them.
